text:
raj: Hey team, POC with Acme just hit a hard blocker. Private endpoint requests fail TLS handshake for some customers only. They see 495/SSL errors and our SDK gets a timeout. Can someone triage?

tyler: Can you paste the client-side error and any server logs? Is this across regions or single VPC?

raj: Repro in us-west-2 only. Client error: `tls: handshake failure` then `context deadline exceeded` after ~8s. From support logs: 
```
2026-03-18T15:04:12Z outbound: connection reset
tls: unable to get local issuer certificate
OCSP: request timed out
```
tyler: hmm OCSP timeout + unable to get local issuer usually points to egress or DNS. Are they using a resolver that returns private IPs for our public OCSP responder?

olga: Confirmed split-horizon failure is common on customer-side. When our private endpoint is present, DNS for ocsp.example-ca.com resolves to 10.100.1.5 (internal) and that's not reachable from the private endpoint container. Firewall is dropping egress to 10.100.1.0/24.

olga: Quick checks: 1) `dig ocsp.example-ca.com @<their-resolver>` 2) `openssl s_client -connect ocsp.example-ca.com:80 -status -servername ocsp.example-ca.com` — ask them to run both from the host that initiates the request to our endpoint.

raj: They're on a managed VPC with outbound restrictions. Customer says firewall denies 10.100.1.0/24 to our subnet. They expect us to support an internal OCSP proxy.

mira: For enterprise POCs we need to clarify two things for the security questionnaire and pricing: if they require an internal OCSP proxy or egress allowances we treat as a networking requirement — may need Private (dedicated) plan or our managed egress addon. Did they sign up for Dedicated?

raj: Not yet — they are evaluating. Pricing question from procurement: extra cost for private egress / VPN. I told them it might be an add-on. Can finance confirm estimated uplift?

tyler: From a triage perspective, workaround options: 1) customer adds DNS override to resolve ocsp.example-ca.com to a reachable proxy (not ideal), 2) we support an option to disable OCSP checking at the client for the POC (security risk, needs approval), 3) run our endpoint in their VPC (Private deployment) so TF rules allow egress to their OCSP responder.

olga: Also check SNI — their TLS inspector rewrites SNI for outbound and sometimes fails SNI-to-cert mapping. If `openssl s_client` with `-servername` passes but our runtime fails, we should capture the raw TLS handshake. Ask them to capture `tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap tcp and host ocsp.example-ca.com` and share with security redacted.

raj: I'll ask for dig + openssl output and the pcap. Also looping in procurement: @mira can you attach a short note about the Private add-on pricing and security approval path?

mira: Sure. For pricing: Private deployment starts at a baseline monthly platform fee + reserved throughput — typical uplift for managed egress is ~20-30% on top of baseline. I'll put actual numbers in a follow-up. For the questionnaire: we can accept customer-managed OCSP proxy but need an architecture diagram + IP allowlist.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-0423 — "POC Acme private endpoint TLS/OCSP failures" assigned to eng-netops.

tyler: Cool. If they can provide the `dig` and `openssl s_client` outputs, plus whether the resolver returns RFC1918 addresses for public OCSP hosts, we can recommend the least-invasive path. If they prefer no changes to their firewall, private deployment with a short-term trial is the fastest route.

raj: Thanks — sending checklist to customer now: `dig`, `openssl s_client -status`, `pcap`, and confirm whether they can allow egress to the CA's OCSP IP or run an internal proxy. Will update thread with their outputs. :thumbsup:
